lines.text: California law hands a probate lawyer $21,000 on this $900K house.
lines.say: California law hands a probate lawyer twenty-one thousand dollars on this house.

lines.text: Say the estate is a $900,000 house. Here's how the law gets to $21,000.
lines.say: Say the estate is a nine hundred thousand dollar house. Here's how the law gets there.

lines.text: Most states just require a 'reasonable' fee. California sets percentages.
lines.say: Most states just require a reasonable fee. California sets percentages.

lines.text: 4% of the first $100,000, 3% of the next $100,000, 2% of the next $800,000, then 1% up to $10 million.
lines.say: It's four percent of the first hundred thousand, three percent of the next hundred thousand, two percent of the next eight hundred thousand, then one percent up to ten million.
So that's four thousand, plus three thousand, plus fourteen thousand: twenty-one thousand.

lines.text: The fee rises with the estate.
lines.say: The fee rises with the estate.

lines.text: But the rate drops from 4% to about 2.3% at $1 million.
lines.say: But the rate drops from four percent to about two point three percent at a million.

lines.text: The twist: it uses gross value. Owe $500,000 on it, and the fee still counts all $900,000.
lines.say: The twist: it uses gross value. Owe five hundred thousand on it, and the fee still counts all nine hundred thousand.

lines.text: The executor can claim the same: another $21,000.
lines.say: The executor can claim the same: another twenty-one thousand.

lines.text: Extra work needs a judge's OK, and living trust assets skip probate.
lines.say: Extra work needs a judge's okay, and living trust assets skip probate.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: California law gives a probate lawyer $21,000 on this house
post.ig:
California law hands a probate lawyer $21,000 on a $900,000 house.

The schedule: 4% of the first $100,000, 3% of the next $100,000, 2% of the next $800,000, then 1% up to $10 million.
Example: a $900,000 house means a $21,000 attorney fee, and the executor can claim another $21,000.
The fee uses gross value, so a mortgage doesn't lower it.

Sources: California Probate Code sections 10800, 10810 and 10811.
